state:
Goal `core-session`, stage 2. Every `Core\Session` member except `start` has all its feature proofs: about, three examples, an attack, a bench with a recorded figure, a Rust `covers:` test and a card in the plain voice. `Core\Session` has a class card. `start` still owes examples, hostile, perf and a Rust `covers:` test, and its card is not yet in the plain voice. Once `start` lands, the `dossier-core-session` check should be green.

Every Session proof needs a real store and a real request. The shape is on disk under `docs/examples/core/Session/regenerate/`: an `nvs.toml` in the feature directory that grants `[capabilities.cache] shared`, sets `[session] backend = "shared"` and `[cache.shared] url = "redis://127.0.0.1:16379"`, and a `.nvsr` beside each program. `tests/hostile/core/Session/<member>/` has the same pair. `benches/members/core/Session/nvs.toml` already serves every Session bench, so a new bench needs only its own `.nvs` and `.nvsr`. Redis is `tests/db/compose.yaml`'s service, which the goal's `env.docker` brings up.

A member that talks to the store (`start`, `regenerate`, `destroy`) is tested the way `regenerate_moves_the_record_to_a_new_id_and_forgets_the_old_one` does it: `crate::tests::granting` with a `[cache.shared] url` pointing at the loopback `serving` fake, asserting the refusal with no store first. Such a member costs a round trip per call, so its bench uses a few thousand iterations.

`bun nv proofs --run --show --no-cache --no-perf --id '<member>'` prints what every example, attack and bench actually printed. Read the attack's output with it: the gate only says it survived. After the last Rust edit to `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs`, run `bun nv proofs --verify --id '<member>'` for each member, and `--record-perf --id '<member>'` for each it names stale.

It talks to the store, so the Rust test has the shape of `regenerate_moves_the_record_to_a_new_id_and_forgets_the_old_one` at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs:1927`. Then run the goal's `dossier-core-session` check and the goal's closing gates (`bun nv verify --doc`, `bun nv owners --closes core-session`, `bun nv playbook --closes core-session`).

backlog: Every `set`, `setSecret` and `remove` call decodes and re-encodes the whole session record, so a request with a large session pays O(record) per call. A request with a 10 MB value and 4000 `setSecret` calls took about 40 s. This is by design today (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/session.rs` module doc); a latency question for whoever next owns the session write path, not this goal.
